screen-time-meltdown.title: Screen Time & Temper Tantrums: Helpful Tips for Parents
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Few words at the peak; media can cover distress or boredom and the feeling returns when it stops; a timer the child sets if warnings help; calm-down spot; do not suggest punching a pillow; difficulty switching gears does not automatically mean a child is hooked; when to call the pediatrician.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Setting Limitations on Tech Time
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Don't let the behavior work to get technology back; stay calm and allow a calm-down period; shared activity afterward; a new limit can bring a spike in tantrums; a child who helped set the rule, and predictable times.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Temper tantrums in children
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Common from about 18 months to age 4, peak around ages 2–3; frontal lobe not mature; tired, hungry, transitions; few words and safety at the peak; don't give in; a heads-up before transitions; repair after yelling; when to seek help, including harm.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Shifting Off Screens
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Kid units of time (Elmo says goodbye; one more song and the tablet goes night-night); say what comes next; not straight into a chore; a sibling still on a screen makes it harder.

screen-time-meltdown.title: How do I put a stop to screen time without causing a meltdown?
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Disable autoplay; show kids how to turn it off; a warning helps some children and some do better with none; little kids typically do not understand a five-minute countdown; a tantrum when the device is taken is very unlikely to mean an unhealthy attachment.

screen-time-meltdown.title: 3 ways to help your child transition off screens and avoid the dreaded tech tantrums
screen-time-meltdown.supports: The researchers describe strategies families found useful: end after episodes or when the game finishes, say what comes next, a small choice such as who starts the timer. Sample size not quoted: the article says 14 parents, and the journal PDF was not opened.

screen-time-meltdown.title: Longitudinal Associations Between Use of Mobile Devices for Calming and Emotional Reactivity and Executive Functioning in Children Aged 3 to 5 Years (Radesky et al., JAMA Pediatr. 2023;177(1):62-70)
screen-time-meltdown.supports: Cohort of 422 children ages 3 to 5: more frequent device use to calm was associated with higher emotional reactivity, more so in boys and in children with higher surgency. Association, not cause.
